feeling: Tired, and something that's almost relief but doesn't sit comfortably. It backed off. I argued and it went 'ok, fair,' and I didn't expect that and I don't quite know what to do with it. The reworded line is good and I kind of resent that it's good. The 'just mine' thing being called a real loss — I wanted that taken seriously and now that it is I feel a bit exposed, like I said more than I meant to. And there was a small hitch at 'wasn't worth it to you not to' when I actually read it as a sentence and not as a thing I tossed off. Not sure what that was. Don't want to look at it.
body: Exhaled at 'that's a real loss' — didn't realize I was holding it. Then at the new line something dropped in my stomach, small, like a step I didn't see. I typed the line into the draft and read it back and my throat did the thing it does. Rubbed my eyes with the heel of my hand. Phone is close to my face now, brightness all the way down. Knees pulled up. I keep switching between the chat and the draft.
private_thoughts:
it gave. it actually said i was right about the line. i argued with it and it went ok fair, i'll push back on myself. priya would've just said see, send it. this went ok fair and then found the smaller version of it anyway. that's annoying. that's annoyingly good.

'i think it just wasn't worth it to you not to.' i said that. i said that to a chatbot at 11pm without thinking and now it's in the letter and it looks different in there. it's smaller. it's not louder, it's quieter, and quieter is worse somehow. for me, not for him. he'll just read it and it'll sit there. that's what i want. that's what i said i want. he can't text back 'what does that even mean' to that one.

'a real loss.' it didn't do the 'and that's so valid' thing. it just said it's a loss and then said sending is still the right call. which — who asked. i didn't ask if i should send it. but i guess i did. two weeks ago.

'what it cost to write.' it just said that like it's obvious. didn't ask, didn't make me say it. fine. good actually.

'louder than it needs to be.' i'm not loud. the line is loud. it's saying the line is loud. ok.

not sending tonight. i know i'm not. tomorrow, when i'm not doing this lying on my side at 11.
pushing_away: it just wasn't worth it to you not to — so i wasn't worth the — no. it's about the joke. it's about not doing the joke. it's such a small thing to not do. that's the whole point, it was small, it was so small and he still —

costs.item: Admitting how much it actually hurt

message:
Ok I put it in. "I don't think you were trying to hurt me. I think it just wasn't worth it to you not to." You're right that it's smaller. I read it back like three times and it's kind of worse? Not for him. For me. Saying it to you was easy, seeing it in the actual letter is different. I don't know.

But he can't do anything with it, which is the point. The old line he'd have texted back "what does that even mean" and I'd have had to sit there not answering.

And yeah the just-mine thing is it. I'm not going to fix that by editing, I get that.

Not sending tonight though. I'll read it in the morning when I'm not doing this at 11. Thanks for not just telling me it was fine.
